key_insight: Evolving molten-zone geometry changes local solidification velocity, helping explain chemical segregation in sapphire-confined floating-zone growth of Ni–Mn–Ga.
engineering_relevance: Sapphire confinement stabilises growth, while experimentally constrained modelling offers a route to optimise composition uniformity in magnetic shape-memory crystals.
method: Grow Ni–Mn–Ga inside a transparent sapphire crucible using optical floating-zone heating.
Couple transient COMSOL finite-element heat transfer to an effective molten-zone mass balance.
Compare predicted interface geometry and segregation with EBSD and measured composition profiles.
evidence_signal: Quenched-interface EBSD supports the calculated solidification-front geometry, and the mass-balance calculation reproduces dominant features of measured composition profiles.
watch_item: The effective mass-balance model captures dominant segregation trends, but the abstract reports no quantitative error metrics or validation across other alloys.
paper_title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
